# Photo Challenge

A Skill Harbor house build: Photo Challenge, the rolling photo game, refereed by your own Muse inside a group chat you own. Each cycle, the referee announces a theme that anyone can photograph without special equipment, something red, my favourite corner, the contents of a pocket. The 3 to 12 registered players then have a fixed window, four days in the default seven day cycle, to take their own photo and submit it. The season ranking rewards regularity, not one evening of glory, and a theme bank plus member suggestions keep the themes fresh.

Collection is deferred and private, and that choice is the heart of the game. Each player sends their photo in a one to one message to the referee, never in the thread during the submission window, and the referee answers with a bare acknowledgement and no comment on the photo, ever. When submissions close, all accepted photos are republished together, in a random order, each under a letter and without its author name while anonymity is on. Nobody collects reactions while the others are still photographing, and nobody votes for a person instead of a photo. The referee never judges taste: whether a photo embodies the theme well is exactly what the vote decides. A submission can be set aside only if it is manifestly unrelated to the theme, through a bounded procedure with a written reason and the host approval, and doubt always keeps the photo.

Voting is by reactions on the photos themselves, two per voter by default, at most one per...
